newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to expand communications services - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to expand communications services - WSJ.

text.p: AT&T Corp is expected to announce Wednesday an expansion of voice, data, paging and electronic mail services to 40 of the biggest markets in the United States with a combined total of more than 70 million people, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The newspaper said Wednesday the new offering, called AT&T Digital PCS (personal communications services), brings together several functions in a single telephone, eliminating the need for a pager or computer.
Citing a company memorandum, it said AT&T planned to "rapidly expand" the new offering to 80 percent of the country covering about 212 million people.
The company would offer the service package at $24.99 a month, the newspaper said.

Users would be able to go about as they pleased with the telephone and call from anywhere for a flat charge of $0.60 a minute, it said, adding that the phones would use batteries with a longer life span, lasting up to 60 hours.
The report confirmed comments made by an industry analyst who told Reuters on Tuesday that the company would launch its next generation digital PCS.
